clue.text: A quarter lit up when cold-shouldered

parts.note: a quarter is one of the compass points, here S for south
lit up means lighted, set alight

explanation.surface: A row flares up when someone is snubbed.
explanation.walkthrough: The page as scanned reads 'quarrel', but only 'quarter' (a compass point, S) gives the wordplay; the two words differ by two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To be cold-shouldered is to be snubbed or treated with disdain, a synonym for being insulted.

clue.text: Emphasise need for second lock

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Insisting that a second lock be fitted to a door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lock' is a lock of hair, not a door lock.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay stress on a point is to accent or underline it.

clue.text: Pass on some grim particulars

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Relay a few gruesome details.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass on news is to communicate or convey it.

clue.text: Appeared reluctant, but suspended a footballer

parts.note: hung means suspended from above
a back is a defensive football player

explanation.surface: Looked hesitant, but a player was banned from matches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspended' reads as a sporting ban, but it means hung up.
explanation.definitionFit: To hang back is to hesitate or hold back from acting.

clue.text: She's English and retiring

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the word and is read in reverse

explanation.surface: She is a shy Englishwoman.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name stands for a woman, any 'she'.

clue.text: Backing an artist shows recognition of merit

indicators.note: backing tells us to read the word for the artist from right to left

parts.note: a drawer is someone who draws, an artist

explanation.surface: Financial support for a painter demonstrates that their talent is acknowledged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' looks like sponsorship but tells you to turn DRAWER round.
explanation.definitionFit: A prize or bonus given for good work is a form of recognition of merit.

clue.text: All a person has left set out with a note attached

indicators.note: out signals the letters of set are spread out and rearranged

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A will's assets are laid out with an attached memo.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead person's property and money together make up their legacy, all they leave behind.

clue.text: Getting a five and making a blunder in declaring

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
erring means making a mistake

explanation.surface: Receiving a handful and slipping up in a statement.
explanation.walkthrough: The scanned page reads 'few', but the wordplay needs 'five' (V).
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to assert or state positively, so it means declaring.

clue.text: Let off school — filling in time

indicators.note: filling in tells us the school goes inside the word for time

parts.note: a date is a point in time
Eton is a famous English public school

explanation.surface: Excused from school, filling in a gap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let off' looks like 'excused', but it means set off a bomb.
explanation.definitionFit: To explode a bomb or firework is to set it off.

clue.text: One joining a writer in a round and getting mellow

indicators.note: in places the joined pair of pieces inside the word for a round

parts.note: a ring is a circle, a round shape
one is the Roman numeral I
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: Someone joins an author in a boxing ring and grows more relaxed.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit that is maturing becomes soft and sweet, i.e. mellow.

clue.text: Attending big match, swear!

parts.note: to be at an event is to attend it
a Test is a major international cricket match

explanation.surface: A spectator at a big game lets out an oath.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test match is an international cricket fixture, a big match in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: To swear to something is to vouch for it formally, to bear witness.

clue.text: Turner's tops. Brown too

definitions.note: Turner's is read as 'Turner is', with the 's a link

parts.note: caps are tops, as on bottles
tan is a brown colour

explanation.surface: Praise for Turner's paintings, and for Brown's.
explanation.walkthrough: The painters Turner and (Ford Madox) Brown mislead: a capstan is a revolving drum that turns to wind rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's revolving winch rotates to haul cable, so it is something that turns.

clue.text: The holy man, awful bore, called for special lighting

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint, a holy man

indicators.note: awful signals that the letters of bore are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: A dreary saint asked for some unusual illumination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The holy man' is a saint, abbreviated in the usual way; 'awful' is the anagram signal, not a comment on the bore.
explanation.definitionFit: A flashing lamp used in discos and photography is a special kind of lighting effect.

clue.text: Found smooth but quite rigid

parts.note: to found metal is to cast it in a mould
to iron cloth is to smooth it

explanation.surface: Discovered calm, yet actually very stiff.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan or alibi that is unbreakable is called so, figuratively meaning firm and inflexible.

clue.text: Choice may be given without thanks

indicators.note: may be suggests the letters could be reorganised into another word

parts.note: ta is informal British for thanks

explanation.surface: A selection may be handed over without a thank-you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means 'with ... outside': GIVEN and TA together are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Vintage wine is of high quality, so the adjective means select or top-grade.

clue.text: Disappearance of box see management about it

indicators.note: about it means the jumbled letters go round the box word, the 'it' pointing back to box
management signals that the letters of see are handled and rearranged

parts.note: to box someone's ears is to clip them

explanation.surface: A theatre box vanishes when the bishop's office takes charge of it.
explanation.walkthrough: SEE rearranged by 'management' gives ESE, which goes 'about it' (CLIP) to make E-CLIP-SE.
explanation.definitionFit: When the moon passes in front of the sun, the sun's vanishing from view is that event.

clue.text: How the woolly-minded use needles

parts.note: people working with wool use needles to make garments, and the woolly-minded are those with wool on their minds

explanation.surface: A dig at muddle-headed people and their pointed tools.
explanation.definitionFit: Knitters work wool into fabric with a pair of needles, so this is literally what they do.

clue.text: Greased say when confined, to bed

indicators.note: confined means held within, so the word for say is enclosed by bed

parts.note: to utter is to say

explanation.surface: Smeared with oil, one says 'when' while bedridden.
explanation.definitionFit: Spreading a fat over bread or a pan means it has been oiled.

clue.text: Separate French articles about a tour de force

indicators.note: about signals the two articles go around the triumph

parts.note: un and le are French articles, the indefinite and definite
a coup is a brilliant feat, a tour de force

explanation.surface: Divide French texts about a masterpiece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' looks like essays, but it is grammar: UN and LE.
explanation.definitionFit: To detach two linked railway carriages is to disconnect them.

clue.text: Flag to stop 'on a 'road

parts.note: to stand is to stop still
RD is the abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: A banner instructs drivers to halt on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophes are print noise; read 'Flag to stop on a road'.
explanation.definitionFit: A banner or ensign carried in battle is a flag.

clue.text: Vessels built by nautical men in America

indicators.note: in tells us the sailors go inside the abbreviation for America

parts.note: US is the United States of America
RN is the Royal Navy, the nautical men

explanation.surface: Ships constructed by American sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: Vases or containers for ashes or tea are vessels in the sense of receptacles.

clue.text: The last to be engaged in underhand activity

indicators.note: to be engaged suggests the words are put to work and rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: The final person is going to be hired for some sneaky business.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting by furtive, secret means is covert, sneaky behaviour.

clue.text: Crusoe's disastrous voyage

indicators.note: disastrous suggests the name has been wrecked and rearranged

parts.note: the possessive s is not a letter of the fodder

explanation.surface: Robinson Crusoe's ill-fated journey ending in shipwreck.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's route or passage is its path through the sea, a journey.

clue.text: Providing the school-head with a home is most sensible

parts.note: the head of school is its first letter, S
a nest is a bird's home

explanation.surface: Giving the headteacher a house is the wisest move.
explanation.definitionFit: Most rational in mind, the superlative of being reasonable.

clue.text: A landlord involved in correspondence

definitions.meaning: a landlord is one who lets property
correspondence here is a written message sent by post

explanation.surface: A property owner caught up in exchanging mail.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who rents out property lets it; a written message posted is correspondence.

clue.text: Painstaking, even if unprepared

parts.note: tho' is a short form of though, meaning even if
rough means unfinished, not prepared

explanation.surface: Careful work, despite not being ready.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone thorough is meticulous and careful, taking pains over every detail.

clue.text: A tenant in time sees certain material advantages

indicators.note: sees is read as 'holds within view', the answer lying inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A renter eventually notices some financial benefits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A tenant in time' is a prisoner doing time; the run sits across 'certain material', and 'advantages' completes the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner serving a sentence occupies a cell, a jailbird's tenancy.

clue.text: Look for sound support

indicators.note: sound tells us the word for support is heard, not spelt

parts.note: a pier is a pillar supporting a bridge

explanation.surface: Searching for good, solid backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like 'solid' but signals a homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: To peer is to gaze closely, a way of looking.

clue.text: Military personnel left to present themselves for duty

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a body of British military personnel
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Soldiers who have departed must turn up for work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like 'departed', but it is the nautical PORT.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers are said to arrive and announce their arrival for duty, the military sense of turning up.

clue.text: Being nice about a large number falling off

indicators.note: about indicates that the nice word wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: decent means nice, respectable
D is the Roman numeral for 500, a large number

explanation.surface: Being pleasant to a crowd that is dwindling.
explanation.definitionFit: A decadent society is in decline, falling off from former standards.

clue.text: Dredge the river and shut up

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
to pen an animal is to shut it up

explanation.surface: Clear out the riverbed and be quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Dredging a channel makes it lower, i.e. increases its depth.

clue.text: Quietly trade or exchange a hunter

parts.note: P is piano, quietly in music

indicators.note: exchange suggests the letters swap places to form a new word

explanation.surface: Discreetly barter or swap with a huntsman.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal that kills and eats others is a hunter by nature.
